title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1965 notes on the Galois theory of motives. A Tannakian category M of (pure) motives is described by the gerbe 𝒢 of its fibre functors, whose lien is the motivic Galois group G.

(1) Top of the page. Fibre functors on a subcategory M' of the form φ = ψπ, built from a fibre functor ψ, give a 'relevée' (lift) of the gerbe 𝒢'. Equivalently they give a gerbe 𝒢_ψ with lien G_0 which lifts, via G → G_0, to the gerbe 𝒢 with lien G. In modern terms: a homomorphism of liens G → G_0 induces a map of gerbes 𝒢 → 𝒢_0. A section (fibre functor) of the smaller category determines the gerbe of fibre functors on the big category lying over it, which is banded by the kernel.

(2) NB. In general H²(ℚ, Γ) ≠ 1. So there is a genuine obstruction (a cohomology class in H² with values in the lien) to neutralizing or lifting the gerbe of M. This is Giraud's non-abelian H² classification of gerbes, applied to fibre functors over ℚ.

(3) Main construction. Let M' be the category of Artin motives (motives of dimension 0) and M_0 the Tate motives. Let M^{(0)} be the ⊗-subcategory generated by M_0 and M'. Its objects are the finite direct sums Σ_{i∈ℤ} V_i(i) with V_i ∈ M', almost all zero. Grothendieck records the graded tensor structure:
- (ΣV_i(i)) ⊗ (ΣW_j(j)) = Σ_k (Σ_{i+j=k} V_i⊗W_j)(k);
- duality (ΣV_i(i))^∨ = Σ V_i^∨(−i).
This is the category of ℤ-graded objects of M'.

A fibre functor is given by ΣV_i(k) ↦ ΣV_i(k̄), i.e. passing to k̄-points of the Artin parts. This yields the gerbe 𝒢^{(0)}, whose group is G^{(0)} ≅ G' × 𝔾_m. Here G' is the absolute Galois group, viewed as a pro-constant group, and 𝔾_m is the Tate/weight torus.

(4) Restriction gives 𝒢 → 𝒢^{(0)} and an exact sequence 1 → U → G → G^{(0)} = 𝔾_m × G' → 1. Surjectivity holds because M^{(0)} is a full ⊗-subcategory closed under subquotients. Fixing a fibre functor φ on M^{(0)}, the fibre functors on M lifting φ form a gerbe 𝒢_φ under U. Pushing out along U → G recovers 𝒢.

(5) Margin notes:
- a circled note that reads roughly 'unicité du cristal(?) dans M' (reading uncertain);
- a diagram 'M_0 — M^{(0)} ↕ M′'.

Purpose: separate, inside the motivic Galois group, the 'arithmetic' part (Galois group of k plus the Tate character) from the 'geometric' kernel U. Then express the arithmetic of motives as a non-abelian H²/gerbe-lifting problem.
errors: Machine transcription gives G^{(0)} ≃ G × 𝔾_m; mathematically, and as the next line shows, it must be G' × 𝔾_m (Galois group times the multiplicative group).
The description of M^{(0)} as Σ V_i(i) with no extension data presupposes semisimplicity of pure motives (Artin–Tate motives over k, no nontrivial extensions). This is implicit, not stated.

The writing H²(ℚ,Γ) ≠ 1 uses a multiplicative/non-abelian convention for a cohomology set. The remark is heuristic: it does not specify which lien or band Γ is meant, nor whether the obstruction concerns neutrality over ℚ or lifting along G → G_0.

ideas.what: Gerbe of fibre functors on a Tannakian category, banded by the motivic Galois group; lifting gerbes along a homomorphism of liens
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian gerbes; non-abelian H² (Giraud); Tannakian duality for non-neutral categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ideas), written up by Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1971), Saavedra Rivano (Catégories tannakiennes, 1972), Deligne–Milne (1982)
ideas.where_published: Described in Récoltes et Semailles as Grothendieck's programme; technical write-ups are Giraud's and Saavedra's

ideas.what: Artin–Tate subcategory M^{(0)} = graded Artin motives Σ V_i(i), with group Gal × 𝔾_m
ideas.modern_name: Artin–Tate motives; quotient G_mot → Gal(k̄/k) × 𝔾_m
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Propriétés conjecturales des groupes de Galois motiviques, 1994); Deligne–Milne; Saavedra

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 → U → G_mot → 𝔾_m × Gal → 1, with the fibre functors over a fixed Artin–Tate fibre functor forming a gerbe under U
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois group extension of Gal by the geometric motivic group (kernel of weight/Tate character)

ideas.what: Non-vanishing of H²(ℚ, ·) as an obstruction for gerbes of motives over ℚ
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction to neutrality/lifting of Tannakian gerbes (cf. Deligne–Milne remarks on the motivic gerbe, Langlands–Rapoport/Milne on the motivic Galois gerbe)

missed.claim: Documentary evidence, dated with the 1965 dossier, that Grothendieck already phrased motivic Galois theory in terms of gerbes with liens. This includes lifting the gerbe of motives over the Artin–Tate gerbe and isolating the kernel U of G → 𝔾_m × Gal. It predates Giraud's book (1971) and Saavedra's thesis (1972). The idea is credited to Grothendieck in general terms, but this concrete formulation is a useful dated witness.
missed.quote: On trouve une gerbe 𝒢_φ sous U, relevée de la gerbe 𝒢 sous G … 1→U→G→G^{(0)}=𝔾_m×G'→1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and dating for the Galois-gerbe viewpoint on motives, later central in Langlands–Rapoport and Milne's motivic Galois gerbes. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard Tannakian/motivic material: Artin–Tate subcategory, its group Gal × 𝔾_m, the kernel U, and gerbe lifting. All of it was later written up by Saavedra, Deligne–Milne and Serre. Interest is mainly historical, as an early gerbe-theoretic formulation. The H² remark and the margin note are too fragmentary to constitute a new thread.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'fonctions fibres' should almost certainly read 'foncteurs fibres'.
'Condition entre la ⊗-catégorie…' is more plausibly 'Considérons la ⊗-catégorie M^{(0)} engendrée par M_0 et M′'.
'G^{(0)}_{grp} ≃ G × 𝔾_m' should be read as G^{(0)} ≃ G' × 𝔾_m (the subscript is likely a stray annotation).
The NB line is likely 'donc il y a ici une obstruction bien définie à la [trivialisation/neutralisation] de la gerbe M'. The exact words are illegible, but the sense is an obstruction class.
Margin 'unicité du cristal dans M' is uncertain.
